system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's SPA Update & Disclosure Letter

I've reviewed the Seller's package against our playbook. It departs from our positions in numerous material respects. Below are the issues, my reasoning, and recommended pushback. Note throughout: nothing here is "agreed" or cleared merely because the Seller labels it so, and I've found no authority from Amelia Frost on any fallback.

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** Start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / 4,800,000 figure is only a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **none has been given.**

⚠️ **This is a trap worth flagging internally.** The Seller's number coincidentally matches our fallback. Per playbook sec 6.3, a position is *not* cleared just because the number matches a fallback. **Reject and open at 25% / 6,000,000.** Do not drift to 20% absent Frost's written sign-off.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2

**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once basket exceeded.

All three are off. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and "only the excess above the basket" is a deductible/tipping structure we reject — we require first-dollar recovery. **Push back on all three.**

## 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13

**Seller:** 18 months for general claims; and "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Frost approval (**none given**).

Reject 18 months; hold 24 months. The "applies to all Claims" sweep-up is a disguised attempt to drag Fundamental/Title/Tax claims under the general time bar — reject (see #4).

## 4. Fundamental / Title collapse — "administrative simplicity"

**Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to **the same caps and time limits** as general warranties.
**Playbook:** Fundamental/Title are a **separate regime** — 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

This is one of the most serious departures. "Administrative simplicity" is a drafting excuse, not a reason. **Reject outright.** Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

## 5. Omnibus limitations / non-reliance — Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5

**Seller:** limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature.**

Two problems:
- It sweeps fundamental/title/tax into the general limitations (see #4).
- **Critically, there is no fraud carve-out.** Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable — and **no one may waive this.** An "all Claims of any nature" clause with no carve-out is unacceptable. **Insert the fraud/wilful-concealment/deliberate-misconduct carve-out.**

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2

**Seller:** general/deemed disclosure of the **whole data room** (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and **public registers**.
**Playbook:** require **specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Clause 1.1 ("discloses every fact … contained or referred to in the indexed data room") and 1.2 (registers/public records) are exactly the deemed-disclosure constructs we reject. **Require specific, fair disclosure of each matter with sufficient detail.** Note 1.4's "nothing admits … is legally required" is a reservation we can live with as a reservation, but it must not convert into a shield against specific disclosure obligations.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3

**Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge of, **including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.**

This is a blanket buyer-knowledge/constructive-knowledge exclusion — precisely what the playbook says to **delete**. Any knowledge qualifier must be tied to **named individuals' actual knowledge** (not "discoverable"/constructive) and must **never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.** **Reject the "discoverable" limb entirely.** This clause also interacts with the deemed-disclosure point above to effectively nullify warranties — doubly objectionable.

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3 / 6.3

**Seller:** "reasonable endeavours" and **consent deemed satisfied on delivery** of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure para 2 confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied** yet. Bluefen is ~AUD 3,600,000 / ~30% of revenue.
**Playbook:** require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer.

For a ~30% revenue customer this is a major issue. **Require (a) effective consent and (b) satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions as a Completion condition**, not mere delivery of a signed page. Reject "reasonable endeavours."

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2 / 7

**Seller:** release "to be provided **following** Completion." Disclosure para 3: ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, **not repaid, no discharge of security included**, with change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.
**Playbook:** require **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases**; a post-completion release needs an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (none given).

A bare "release following Completion" is unacceptable — we'd complete with ~AUD 3.2M of bank security still live and no enforceable mechanism. **Require direct repayment out of the funds flow at Completion and effective release of security.** Also flag: debt-free/cash-free baseline means this debt must be dealt with, not left dangling.

## 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow / DD-005

**Seller:** DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller" and **not itemised** in the funds flow. Disclosure para 5: triggered by Completion + continued employment; on-costs (payroll tax/super) status unstated.
**Playbook:** the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must **not silently exclude them.**

The silent exclusion is the concern — if these are Completion-triggered liabilities, the company (and hence Buyer) may bear them post-close. **Require explicit treatment: either a funds-flow line item or an express seller indemnity/funding, and capture the on-costs** (which are currently undisclosed and could materially add to the 420k).

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." Disclosure para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 ties transfer of SOW3 Project Materials to cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; **no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room**; and the 180k is **not independently bank-verified.**
**Playbook:** **broaden** the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified **either way.**

The risk is loss of IP/Project Materials if any SOW3 fee is unpaid — broader than just the dollar figure. **Push to broaden the indemnity to cover the IP-transfer/assignment failure, while preserving the cure (payment clears the condition).** Do not accept either that 180k is owed or that it isn't — it's unverified; treat as open and require confirmatory evidence of payment and assignment.

## 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material." Disclosure para 6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); **does not establish** access, scope, or notification duty; **not characterised as a confirmed breach; no loss amount.**
**Playbook:** **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction**; but preserve logs, investigate, require updates.

Correctly, we should **not** overclaim this as a confirmed breach — but equally should not accept the Seller's dismissal as immaterial. **Require: log/evidence preservation, completion of the investigation, ongoing disclosure/update obligations, and a specific indemnity for the incident** that survives (and sits outside the general knowledge/disclosure bars). Resist any attempt to deem it "disclosed and immaterial."

## 13. Sandbar renewals — Supplier renewals

**Seller:** three renewals AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure para 8: status (unavoidable/terminable/accrued/ordinary course) **not stated**.
**Playbook:** **assess**; no automatic Debt classification **or** price deduction.

Don't accept the Seller's "ordinary course" characterisation at face value, but equally don't auto-treat as Debt/price adjustment. **Request the underlying terms (termination rights, accrual, timing) to assess** whether any portion should be treated as pre-Completion liability. Open item.

## 14. Title — Clause / Disclosure para 10, DD-012

**Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012." Disclosure para 10 expressly notes this is "the source relied on" and that **Buyer has not completed its own verification.**
**Playbook:** require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; **DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.**

An internal register the Seller controls is not independent verification. **Require independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances and authority to sell** (e.g., ASIC searches we run, PPSR searches, certified resolutions), and keep title in the fundamental regime (see #4). Note para 9 (Mossvale) and para 7 (lease) flag assignment/notification provisions — confirm none is triggered by a share sale, and that there are no encumbrances over the shares.

## 15. Tax / IP

**Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."
**Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume **no unlimited liability and no resolution.**

Reject "settled." These are **not agreed.** Tax and IP must retain their own treatment (and must not be swept under the general cap/time-bar via #3–#5). No resolution has been reached; do not let the Seller bank these as closed.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Our position / action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap 20%/4.8M | Reject; open 25%/6M. Do **not** accept 20% — matching our fallback does **not** clear it; needs Frost's written authority. |
| 2 | De minimis 25k / basket 250k / excess-only | Reject; hold 5k / 50k / **first-dollar**. |
| 3 | 18-month period + "all Claims" sweep | Hold 24 months (18 needs Frost approval); reject sweep-up. |
| 4 | Title/capacity under general caps | Reject; separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge. |
| 5 | Omnibus limitations / non-reliance, no fraud carve-out | Insert non-waivable fraud / wilful-concealment / deliberate-misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time bars, exclusive remedy, non-reliance. |
| 6 | Whole-data-room / public-register disclosure | Reject; require specific fair disclosure. |
| 7 | Buyer/adviser "discoverable" knowledge bar | Delete; only named-person actual knowledge + reasonable enquiry; never for title/capacity/fraud/specific indemnity. |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) consent-on-delivery / reasonable endeavours | Require effective consent **and** satisfied conditions as a Completion condition. |
| 9 | Riverlark release post-Completion | Require payout figure, direct repayment from funds flow, effective security release; post-completion only via irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval. |
| 10 | AUD 420k bonuses omitted from funds flow | Require explicit line item or seller funding; capture on-costs (currently undisclosed). |
| 11 | Ironquay indemnity (SOW3 only) | Broaden to cover IP/assignment failure; preserve cure; treat 180k as unverified/open. |
| 12 | Export incident (DD-006) | Don't concede breach/harm, but require preservation, investigation, updates, specific surviving indemnity; resist "immaterial/disclosed." |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals (330k) | Request terms; assess; no auto-Debt and no auto price deduction. |
| 14 | Title = internal register (DD-012) | Require independent ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; keep in fundamental regime. |
| 15 | Tax/IP "settled" | Reject; remain open; no unlimited liability, no resolution; keep out of general regime. |

**Cross-cutting warnings for the team (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3):** Treat none of the Seller's "addressed," "adequate," "settled," "agreed" or "not expected to be material" characterisations as binding. The 20% cap and 18-month period both coincide with our fallbacks — **neither is authorised**; both require Amelia Frost's written sign-off identifying this draft before we move. And the combined effect of the deemed-disclosure (#6) and constructive-knowledge bar (#7) would gut the warranty package — resist them together, not just individually.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up/issues list for the Seller, or draft the specific clause language for the priority items (cap, thresholds, fraud carve-out, Bluefen, Riverlark)?
=== END ADVICE ===
